title: When the mean lies and the median saves you

videos.script: Horta has nine people on the payroll. Eight of them pick, pack and deliver. The ninth founded the company. {{payroll}} The eight earn between two thousand one hundred and three thousand four hundred reais a month. The founder takes twenty-eight thousand. {{founder}} Ask for the average salary and you get five thousand three hundred and thirty-nine reais. Eight of the nine people earn less than that. {{mean}} Nobody at Horta earns anything close to the average. It sits in an empty stretch between the staff and the founder, pulled out there by one person. {{empty}} Now take the median. Line the nine salaries up and take the fifth. Two thousand four hundred. That is what a typical employee earns, and the founder could double their pay without moving it. {{median}} This lesson is about that gap. When it opens, what it tells you, and when the mean is still the number you need, even though it describes nobody. {{lesson}}
